solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Will’s gift follows Lorraine’s from official body (8)

indicatorNotes.follows: to follow is to come after, so the gift's letters come after Lorraine's

blocks.note: Lorraine is in France, where 'from' is de
a legacy is what a will leaves you

annotation.surface: A bequest from someone called Lorraine turns up after another from an official body.
annotation.walkthrough: Will and Lorraine look like two people; one is a legal document and the other a French region, so 'Lorraine's from' means the French for from.
annotation.definitionFit: A delegacy is a committee of delegates, such as those a university appoints, so it is a plain synonym for an official body.

entries.clue: Unwanted, half-hearted, pitiable Edward’s upset (2,4)

indicatorNotes.half-hearted: a heart only half there: one of the two central Os of POOR is lost
indicatorNotes.upset: upset means knocked over, and in a down answer that turns the letters upside down

blocks.note: POOR (pitiable) with one of its central Os gone

annotation.surface: Poor Edward is upset at feeling unwanted and only half-hearted.
annotation.walkthrough: The commas make three adjectives for Edward, but only the first is the definition; the upset applies to the whole of POR + TED.
annotation.definitionFit: De trop is a French borrowing for superfluous or in the way, which is what an unwanted guest is.

entries.clue: Little drained river filled by good hose? (7)

indicatorNotes.drained: a drained vessel has lost its contents, so LITTLE loses its inside letters
indicatorNotes.filled by: what fills something goes into it, so G goes inside LE + WEAR

blocks.note: the Wear, a river in north-east England

annotation.surface: A trickle of a river being topped up with a garden hose.
annotation.walkthrough: The drained river and the hose make a gardening picture; the question mark flags that hose here means stockings.
annotation.definitionFit: Hose in the old sense are stockings or tights, so the definition is by example, flagged by the question mark.

entries.clue: Shocking pink ought to get blocked by Head of Rugby making uniform decisions (10)

indicatorNotes.Shocking: a shock jolts things out of place, so the letters of 'pink ought' are jumbled
indicatorNotes.get blocked by: something blocked has an obstruction lodged in it, so R sits inside the jumble

annotation.surface: A rugby club's committee blocks a lurid pink kit and imposes a uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shocking pink' is a colour name, so it resists being split; 'Shocking' is the anagram signal and 'pink' part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Groupthink is a group's drift towards conformity, and the conformity shows in decisions that come out uniform.

entries.clue: Councillor corrects officer, with call for analysis before making advance (6,7)

blocks.note: Cr is the abbreviation for councillor
to ring is to call on the phone

annotation.surface: A councillor edits an officer's report and calls for a review before a military advance.
annotation.walkthrough: The advance sounds military but is a loan; the definition is the whole phrase after 'for'.
annotation.definitionFit: A lender checks a borrower's record before advancing money, and that check is credit scoring: a descriptive definition.

entries.clue: FC Espanyol’s wingers or chap from Barcelona? (6)

indicatorNotes.wingers: wingers play out on the wings, so these are the letters at the two edges of Espanyol

blocks.note: Man U, Manchester United, a football club
E and L, the outside letters of ESPANYOL

annotation.surface: A football question: is this chap a winger for the Barcelona club Espanyol?
annotation.walkthrough: Manuel is the waiter from Barcelona in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers; the question mark admits the definition is one particular chap.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Manuel, the hapless Fawlty Towers waiter, famously comes from Barcelona.

entries.clue: Slip out of large alcove (4)

indicatorNotes.out of: to take something out of a word is to remove it, here L from LAPSE

annotation.surface: Someone slips out of a large alcove.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Slip out of' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'Slip' is LAPSE and 'out of large' removes L.
annotation.definitionFit: An apse is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church, a grand kind of alcove.

entries.clue: Unusually long feature film’s rating dispute entertaining writer? (7)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house, so U + ROW holds NIB

blocks.note: a pen's nib does the writing

annotation.surface: An overlong feature film sparks a quarrel over its rating with a visiting screenwriter.
annotation.walkthrough: The feature film is a false trail: the feature is facial. The question mark covers writer = NIB, the part of a pen that writes.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyebrows are facial features, and a unibrow joins two into one, so it is a feature of unusual length.

entries.clue: People kept inside houses pull up those making slow progress (8)

indicatorNotes.houses: to house something is to give it a place inside, so LAGS takes GARD within
indicatorNotes.up: in a down answer, going up means reading DRAG from the bottom

blocks.note: lags are convicts, kept inside prison

annotation.surface: Prisoners in a jail slow down as they are hauled along.
annotation.walkthrough: Lag is British slang for a convict, usually a hardened old one.
annotation.definitionFit: A laggard is one who lags behind the rest, a plain synonym for a slowcoach.

entries.clue: I appreciate that golf game (3)

blocks.note: G is golf in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A golfer thanks a partner for the game.
annotation.walkthrough: Ta is informal British thanks, the 'I appreciate that' of the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by class: tag, where one child chases and touches the others, is one example of a game.

entries.clue: Problem for schools is forgiven, oddly? Hard to stop it (11)

indicatorNotes.oddly: done oddly means done in a strange way, so 'is forgiven' is written out of order
indicatorNotes.to stop: a stopper plugs a gap, so H is pushed into the jumble

annotation.surface: An education problem where a pupil is let off, which a hard line should stop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' usually asks for odd letters, but here it makes an anagram. The schools are schools of fish, not places of education.
annotation.definitionFit: A school is a shoal of fish, and overfishing strips the sea of them, so it is a problem for schools in that sense.

entries.clue: Complaint affecting consumer goods — opinion broadcast loudly at first (4,9)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters of 'goods opinion' are scattered
indicatorNotes.at first: at first means at the start, where F is placed

annotation.surface: A consumer complains about faulty goods and airs a loud opinion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Consumer goods' is a stock phrase, but the definition ends at 'consumer'; 'goods' is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Complaint is used in its medical sense of illness, and food poisoning strikes whoever consumed the bad food.

entries.clue: Upfront in struggling with pros and cons here (4,6)

indicatorNotes.struggling: something struggling twists and writhes, so 'in' and 'pros' are twisted into a new order

annotation.surface: A frank person struggling to weigh the pros and cons of a decision.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pros and cons' is a set phrase, but the pros are anagram fodder and the cons are convicts.
annotation.definitionFit: Cons is slang for convicts, and an open prison, a low-security jail, is where some of them are held.

entries.clue: A number in West Side Story save its opening song (4)

indicatorNotes.save its opening: save means except, so everything but the first letter is kept

blocks.clueFragment: A number in West Side Story
blocks.note: 'Maria' is a song from the musical

annotation.surface: Picking a number from West Side Story, apart from the opening song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Save' means except, not rescue.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by class: an aria is the solo song of opera.

entries.clue: Merchant ship carrying boulders periodically (10)

indicatorNotes.carrying: a ship carrying cargo holds it inside, so WHALER holds the letters
indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular periods, so every other letter of 'boulders'

blocks.note: a whaler is a whaling ship

annotation.surface: A merchant ship loaded with a cargo of rocks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Merchant ship' is a stock phrase, but merchant alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by class: a wholesaler is the kind of merchant who sells in bulk to shops.

entries.clue: Area with great resources but not one sign of McDonald’s (6)

indicatorNotes.but not one: 'but not' excludes, and one is I, so RICHES loses its I

annotation.surface: A resource-rich region with not a single McDonald's to be seen.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a place without a burger bar; 'one sign' actually splits so that one is the missing I.
annotation.definitionFit: McDonald's logo is the golden arches, a yellow M made of two arches, so the definition is a particular sign.

entries.clue: Playmaker during sports day showed contempt (7)

indicatorNotes.during: what happens during an event happens within it, so SHAW sits within PE

blocks.note: George Bernard Shaw, a maker of plays

annotation.surface: A team's playmaker sneered his way through sports day.
annotation.walkthrough: Playmaker sounds like a football term; it is a playwright, Shaw.
annotation.definitionFit: Pshaw! is a scornful exclamation, so to have pshawed is to have voiced contempt: the verb comes from the noise.

entries.clue: Fancied precious metal parts one dug up (8)

indicatorNotes.parts: to part something is to split it, so the metal splits the digging word and sits in the gap

annotation.surface: A prospector fancies the precious metal found where some was dug up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancied' looks like it might go with the precious metal as a desire, but it is the definition, in the sense of pictured in the mind.
annotation.definitionFit: Fancy in the sense of picture or suppose, as in 'fancy that', makes fancied a plain synonym for imagined.

entries.clue: Knight shot on horse in Italian battle (7)

indicatorNotes.on: one thing on another is added to it, so N + GO follows the horse

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse
N, the chess notation for knight
a go = a shot, an attempt

annotation.surface: A knight is shot on horseback in an Italian battle.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word fits the battlefield, but the shot is a go, a turn.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Marengo, in northern Italy, is where Napoleon defeated the Austrians in 1800.

entries.clue: Gag about parent sporting tie lacking originality (7)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so RETCH wraps round MA

annotation.surface: A gag about a parent wearing an unoriginal necktie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sporting tie' pretends to be someone wearing a necktie; it is a sports fixture, and one lacking originality is a repeat.
annotation.definitionFit: A tie is a sports fixture, and a rematch replays one between the same sides, so it is not the original contest.

entries.clue: Misfortunes always in poetry? Too right! (3,3)

blocks.note: ay is a poetic form of aye, ever

annotation.surface: Poetry is always about misfortune, and someone heartily agrees.
annotation.walkthrough: AY (or aye) for always is archaic and mostly found in verse.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are idioms of emphatic agreement, one British-informal and one more general, so they swap in conversation.

entries.clue: Allied countries in a French article in France, say (7)

indicatorNotes.in: one thing in another is inside it, so NATO goes inside A + LE

annotation.surface: An article about the Allies stationed in France.
annotation.walkthrough: France is not the country but the novelist Anatole France; 'say' marks him as one example of an Anatole.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Anatole France was a French novelist, so France is one bearer of the name Anatole.

entries.clue: Favour European up to now (6)

blocks.note: to favour something is to be for it

annotation.surface: Someone has always been pro-European until now.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as politics; 'favour' has to be split as BE FOR.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, as in 'never seen before', before means at any time until now.

entries.clue: Number ones from Simple Minds, say, after Rolling Stones (4)

indicatorNotes.Number ones from: the number one of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.after Rolling: something rolled over ends up facing the other way, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: first letters of Simple and Minds

annotation.surface: A pop chart piece: Simple Minds' number ones, coming after the Rolling Stones'.
annotation.walkthrough: Simple Minds and the Rolling Stones are both bands, and number ones sound like chart hits; the definition hides at the end of a band name.
annotation.definitionFit: Stones is used in the jeweller's sense of precious stones, of which gems is a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Kid’s caught with booze in part of music practice (5,5)

indicatorNotes.with: with means alongside, so the drink is set next to the other pieces

blocks.note: a minor is a kid, plus the 's

annotation.surface: A child is caught drinking during music practice.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Kid's' supplies the S, not a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: Music students play scales daily, minor ones among them, so the definition is one component of practice.

entries.clue: Note gets repeated in soprano’s part (4)

indicatorNotes.gets repeated: repeated means said again, so the note is written a second time

blocks.note: mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A singer keeps repeating one note in her part.
annotation.walkthrough: Mimi is the soprano heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Mimi is the leading soprano role in La Bohème.

entries.clue: Capital area healthy nurses can gate-crash on vacation (7,4)

indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse is to hold close, as a baby, so NOT ILL holds the rest inside
indicatorNotes.on vacation: a vacated house is empty, so the word keeps only its outer letters

blocks.note: GATE-CRASH with its inside emptied, leaving G…H

annotation.surface: Nurses on holiday gate-crash a party in the capital.
annotation.walkthrough: The nurses look like people but it is a container verb. Notting Hill is a district of west London, famous for its carnival.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is by example: Notting Hill is a district of west London, the capital.

entries.clue: India isn’t seen in state that surprises me (3)

indicatorNotes.isn’t seen in: what isn't seen in a word is absent from it, so I is taken out

blocks.note: I is India in the NATO alphabet, removed

annotation.surface: Someone surprised that India is not seen in a particular state.
annotation.walkthrough: India is a country in the surface, a letter in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition spells out what the interjection says: 'oho!' is how a speaker voices that something surprises them.

entries.clue: Cutting funding from the west, I see Liberal making bloomer (6)

indicatorNotes.Cutting: a knife cutting something goes into it, so AH + L goes into the funding word
indicatorNotes.from the west: west is left on a map, so the across word is read from right to left

annotation.surface: A Liberal politician blunders over cuts to Western aid.
annotation.walkthrough: A bloomer sounds like a blunder, which suits the political surface; it is a flower, something that blooms.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: bloomer, literally a thing that blooms, stands for a flower, and the dahlia is one example.

entries.clue: Gave off energy, keeping Anne’s successor in pain (8)

indicatorNotes.off: food gone off has gone bad, so 'gave' plus E comes out wrong
indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold on to it, so the jumble holds GRI inside

blocks.note: George I, Georgius Rex, who followed Queen Anne

annotation.surface: A radiator gave off heat, keeping the queen's heir in agony.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gave off energy' reads as radiating; 'off' is the anagram signal. George I succeeded Queen Anne in 1714; GR is his royal cipher.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are transitive verbs for causing distress, so 'it will pain her' and 'it will aggrieve her' swap cleanly.
